note: Is the popularity prior load-bearing, or a fragile bet on the public set's popularity profile? Answered by forcing w_popularity on both tracks and re-running all three session pools. The long-tail 800 samples the catalog uniformly (median popularity rank 82) and is the most hostile private set that could plausibly be constructed.
reproduce: set w_popularity on both TRACKS in src/routing.py, then run heldout_eval.run_evaluation() against each pool

conclusion.reading: The prior pays about seven times more when the data matches its assumption than it costs when the data is adversarial, and Hit@10 never falls below 0.967 in any configuration. It is a cheap tiebreaker, not a load-bearing assumption: category routing, slot state and the commit-to-one-pick policy carry the score.
